newsitem.title: UK: Bristol-Myers cancer lead threatened - study.
newsitem.headline: Bristol-Myers cancer lead threatened - study.

text.p: Bristol-Myers Squibb Co's global leadership in cancer drugs will be threatened by patent expiries on a number of key products, management consultancy Datamonitor said on Monday.

Datamonitor said BMS, which currently has five of the top ten-selling cytotoxic cancer drugs, "should retain its leadership position in the cytotoxic market for several years yet, however, its position is likely to be jeopardised by the declining sales of Taxol in particular."
Taxol, which is the biggest selling product in the $3.26 billion annual market for cancer-fighting drugs, loses its patent protection this year, with significant generic competition expected.

Datamonitor said Taxol was also under threat from the growth of similar products, notably Rhone Poulenc Rorer Inc's Taxotere, which is used in breast cancer, and SmithKline Beecham Plc's Hycamtin, used in ovarian cancer.

Datamonitor said BMS was instigating a number of strategies to deal with generic competition. These included a five-year exclusivity deal with U.S. healthcare purchaser VMA, under which VHA members would receive a favourable price on another best-selling drug, Paclitaxel, in exchange for maintaining the drug's market share.
It said other products were also included in the agreement.
Datamonitor said that in the next two years products launched recently buy other companies would overtake some of BMS's leading products in terms of sales value if not volume.

It singled out Eli Lilly & Co's Gemzar for non-small cell lung and pancreatic cancer, Zeneca Group Plc's Tomudex for colorectal cancer, SmithKline's Hycamtin and another colorectal cancer drug Campto/Camptosar, sold by RPR in Europe and Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc in the U.S.
